name: Animals
description: Animals is a hilarious and chaotic reaction game derived from the classic Snap. While standard Snap requires players to shout 'Snap!' when ranks match, Animals requires each player to pick a specific animal and make that animal's sound (or shout its name) when a match occurs. It is a game of pure speed, observation, and auditory focus.

history.origins: Originating as a parlor game variant of Snap in the late Victorian era, Animals became a popular children's party game due to its noisy and interactive nature.
timeline: 1880s: Snap is first marketed by John Jaques & Son.
1920s: Animal-themed decks become common, leading to the specific 'shout the sound' variant.
Present: Highly popular in early childhood education for developing pattern recognition and reaction time.
history.cultural: A classic 'Icebreaker' game used to lower inhibitions through silly noises.
history.evolution: The game shifted from simple rank-observation to social-observation, as you must now associate a card match with a specific player's chosen identity.

setup.players: 3-6 players. Each player MUST choose a distinct animal (e.g., Cat, Dog, Cow, Rooster) and tell the others.
setup.dealing: The entire deck is dealt out face down to the players as evenly as possible. Players keep their cards in a face-down pile and do not look at them.

rules.objective: Finish the deal with the largest pile of cards by being the first of the matching players to call the other player's animal (or noise) when their top cards match in rank.
rules.gameplay: 1. **The Choice**: Each player announces their chosen animal at the start. 2. **Turning**: Starting left of the dealer, each player flips the top card of their face-down pile face-up onto a personal face-up pile. Cards should be flipped AWAY from the player so everyone sees them at once. 3. **The Match**: When any two players' top face-up cards match in rank (e.g., two 8s), the first of those two players to make the OTHER player's animal noise (or shout their animal name) wins the match. 4. **Winning Piles**: The winner of the match takes both face-up piles and places them face-down at the bottom of their draw pile. 5. **Snap Pot (Optional)**: If any non-matching player shouts first, or a player makes a false sound, their face-up pile goes into a center 'Snap Pot'. The first person to identify a match with the Pot wins it.
keyRules: Speed is Everything: If both matching players make the sound at the same time, the first one clearly finished wins.
Identity Crisis: You must make your OPPONENT'S sound, not your own.
Rotation: If you run out of face-down cards, turn your face-up pile over and continue.

strategy.basic: Concentrate on the players to your immediate left and right first, as those are the piles you will see most clearly.
strategy.intermediate: Memorize the animal associated with each player before the first card is even dealt. Repeat them in your head: 'John=Pig, Sarah=Cow...'
strategy.advanced: The 'Wait and Bait': If you see a match, wait a fraction of a second to ensure the opponent doesn't notice first, then bark clearly to claim the pile before they can react.
tips: Select an animal with a very short, sharp sound (like 'Woof!') for an advantage over those who chose 'Cokay-doodle-doo!'.
Keep your hands ready, but not over the cards.

variations.name: The Farmyard Snap
variations.description: Instead of ranks, use a specialized deck where the animals are printed on the cards. You match the animal on the card to the sound you must make.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation is purely thematic; it uses animal-printed cards but keeps the same engine structure and rules.

scoring.description: The game is a capture-style contest where, after the full deck has been dealt and played through, the player who has collected the most cards wins.
scoring.winCondition: The player with the most cards when the deck has been fully dealt and no further cards remain to be turned wins the game.

synthesis.shortDescription: A riotous reaction game where players must make the correct animal noises as soon as the cards match. Fast, loud, and perfect for testing your reflexes and your memory.

hero.tagline: Don't just snap. Bark, Mo-o-o, and Roar your way to victory!
